cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this context may or may not be relevant to your tasks
cards.claim: Claude Code wraps CLAUDE.md in a reminder saying it may be irrelevant, so the model discards sections it deems off-task and the more irrelevant content there is the more it ignores everything.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as the core problem; no measurement in the skill.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md as a whole; explains why 390 lines loses adherence
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — humanlayer/skills created (improve-claude-md); (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Wrap conditionally-relevant sections of the CLAUDE.md in `<important if="condition">` XML tags.
cards.claim: Wrap domain-specific CLAUDE.md sections in <important if="condition"> blocks so the model gets an explicit relevance signal that overrides the 'may not be relevant' framing, keeping everything inline.
cards.evidence_detail: Mechanism described as exploiting the XML-tag pattern in Claude Code's own system prompt; no benchmark given.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: wrap invariant sections (mobile outbox, dispatcher, bill freeze, migrations) in conditional blocks instead of trimming; could be an alternative or companion to the gated trim
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md; (B) March 2026 — skills repo

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if it's relevant to 90%+ of tasks, leave it bare. If it's relevant to a specific kind of work, wrap it.
cards.claim: Keep project identity, project map and tech stack bare at the top; only task-specific guidance gets conditional wrappers (90% relevance rule of thumb).
cards.evidence_detail: Rule of thumb, no data.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md structure: stack table and 'what FixFlow is' stay bare; everything else conditional
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: never group unrelated rules under one broad condition.
cards.claim: Each conditional block needs a narrow, specific trigger; a broad condition like 'writing any code' matches everything and defeats the signal.
cards.evidence_detail: Good/bad examples given (imports, new components, new files each get own trigger).
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md invariants: one trigger per invariant (e.g. 'editing models.py', 'adding an outbox kind', 'enabling the dispatcher')
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Frontier models can reliably follow a few hundred. Claude Code's system prompt and tools already use ~50
cards.claim: Instruction budget: frontier models follow only a few hundred instructions reliably and the Claude Code system prompt already consumes about 50, so the CLAUDE.md must be as lean as possible.
cards.evidence_detail: Numbers stated without source or experiment.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md length budget; supports counting instructions, not lines, when trimming
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md / Writing a good CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Cut any instruction that a linter, formatter, or pre-commit hook can enforce
cards.claim: Delete from CLAUDE.md anything a linter, formatter or pre-commit hook can enforce, and suggest pre-push/pre-commit hooks instead.
cards.evidence_detail: Listed as a trim step (step 7: 'delete linter territory').
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim list; also re-opens the skipped pre-commit gate and hooks decision (mark as re-open)
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: LLMs are in-context learners — if your codebase consistently uses a pattern, the agent will follow it
cards.claim: Cut instructions the agent can discover from existing code patterns, because after a few searches it will follow the codebase's consistent conventions anyway.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as principle.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim criteria for 'Where things live' and per-slice conventions
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Cut code snippets. They go stale and bloat the file.
cards.claim: Replace code snippets in CLAUDE.md with file path references; snippets go stale and bloat.
cards.evidence_detail: Principle only.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: replace inline shapes with pointers (the file already uses path references for most)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not shard into separate files that require the agent to make tool calls to discover
cards.claim: Avoid progressive disclosure into separate files unless the content is very verbose; conditional inline blocks keep everything visible while weighting what matches, so sharding is a last resort.
cards.evidence_detail: Argued as the point of <important if>; contrasts with sharding into docs the agent must go and read.
cards.landing: Decision between trimming CLAUDE.md into docs/ (needs tool calls, may be skipped) versus conditional blocks; relevant to the gated trim and the knowledge-store pilot
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not drop commands from the original file.
cards.claim: Keep all commands, wrapped in a single 'need to run commands' conditional block, because the commands table is foundational reference even if some are rarely used.
cards.evidence_detail: Principle plus worked before/after example (Turborepo).
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md Commands section: one conditional wrapper, never trimmed
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: remove anything like "leverage the X agent" or "follow best practices"
cards.claim: Delete vague instructions that are not concrete and actionable (e.g. 'follow best practices').
cards.evidence_detail: Listed as step 9.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md audit pass for vague lines
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Skip the preamble and keep prose brief. Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear.
cards.claim: To explain code, prefer compact structural views (pseudocode, call tree, component tree, file tree, Mermaid, diff) over prose, choosing the smallest view that answers the question.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill instructions with example snippets for each view type; no measurement.
cards.landing: A show-me style skill in .claude/skills/ for owner-facing explanations; also compact phase summaries in the one-page owner view
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) show-me blog post 2026-08-12; (B) August 2026 skills repo

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use `diff` when the point is what changes and the surrounding shape already exists.
cards.claim: Show change as a diff over the existing shape (component tree, file tree, call tree, pseudocode) and show the whole block only when most of it is new or order matters.
cards.evidence_detail: Four diff examples (component, file layout, call tree, control flow).
cards.landing: Reviewer-facing PR body and the Opus reviewer's brief: structural diff instead of file-by-file changelog

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Keep only the calls, files, props, states, and boundaries needed to answer the user's current question
cards.claim: Place each visual next to the short text it supports and include only the elements needed for the current question; do not use every view type.
cards.evidence_detail: Guidance paragraph.
cards.landing: Owner view / closing message length discipline

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: allow_implicit_invocation: false
cards.claim: show-me is invoked only on explicit user request (disable-model-invocation: true in frontmatter, allow_implicit_invocation false for Codex), so skill descriptions do not compete for the model's attention or fire unasked.
cards.evidence_detail: Config values only; visual-pr uses the same pattern with description 'Only use when the user explicitly invokes this skill by name'.
cards.landing: Frontmatter policy for the skills being added under .claude/skills/: mark owner-only or heavy skills as manual-invocation

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: write one focused HTML file — a diagram, an infographic, or a short slide deck
cards.claim: For dense UI, layout or state comparisons, produce one focused HTML file matched to the product's styling, with real labels and data, and open it for the user.
cards.evidence_detail: Instruction only.
cards.landing: Owner-facing one-page view could be a generated HTML file rather than markdown

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Keep **Why the change** to exactly one sentence.
cards.claim: PR body is a fixed three-part template: Why (exactly one sentence), Special things to note (1-3 reviewer warnings such as migrations, compatibility, deliberate omissions), and a Change outline of structural views.
cards.evidence_detail: Template with strict length limits; 'Do not expand the PR body beyond that template.' Author not visible in files (org only), so tagged other.
cards.landing: Phase routine: shape of the draft-PR body and the Opus reviewer's input (alongside 'Plan @ <sha>' and decisions journal)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: a compact, `/show-me`-inspired structural view rather than prose or a file-by-file changelog.
cards.claim: The change outline must be a structural view (SQL/endpoint contracts, key types, file tree of responsibilities, component trees, call/data flow) with only categories that changed, not a file-by-file changelog.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill instruction.
cards.landing: Reviewer prompt: reviewer reads structure first; PR template for migration/models changes (SQL table and contract view)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Save and publish the description
cards.claim: The PR description is saved as a file in a task directory (.humanlayer/tasks/{slug}/pr-description.md) and pushed with gh pr edit --body-file, so the written description lives in the repo/task record as well as the PR.
cards.evidence_detail: Workflow step 5; falls back to pr-{number}/description.md.
cards.landing: Decisions journal / PR body saved in a known path: gives an auditable artifact that the routine step ran

cards.author: other
cards.quote: [2-3 sentence summary of what the PR does and key implementation decisions]
cards.claim: The agent's closing message is a fixed template: Status (PR link, saved description link, ticket), a 2-3 sentence Summary, Files Changed list, Next Steps.
cards.evidence_detail: Template file.
cards.landing: The six-question closing message: a fixed template makes omissions visible

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Write as one human talking to another: avoid jargon and slang
cards.claim: Write PR text in plain, simple, concise language as one human to another.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line style rule; note this skill also tells the agent to commit, push and create the PR itself if none exists.
cards.landing: Style rule for owner-facing text in the one-page view

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Set point** — the desired end state for some property of the codebase.
cards.claim: Frame recurring agent work as a control loop: set point, sensor (measures the gap), controller (picks the next small change), actuator (coding agent opens a PR), under disturbances (teammates, dependency bumps, generated code), with a human on the loop.
cards.evidence_detail: Conceptual model; one worked example (React Doctor) in a production monorepo, no outcome numbers.
cards.landing: Reusable workflow library: a saved sense-control-act workflow shape for repeated audit/fix tasks (e.g. code-quality sweeps)
cards.inventory_ref: (B) June 2026 — design-control-loop skill added 2026-06-30 by Kyle

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Read the repo before you ask
cards.claim: The designing agent reads CI, package files, validation scripts and existing skills/loops first and comes to the interview with proposals rather than a blank form.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase A instruction.
cards.landing: Skill-authoring convention: explore-then-propose before asking the owner questions

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Make each component runnable locally and standalone before wiring it into CI
cards.claim: Land the sensor and controller as version-controlled scripts the user can run by hand, run the actuator locally via its headless CLI, and only then wire CI, so the workflow is a thin orchestrator of pieces already proven.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase D with completion criterion; also Phase H dry-run via a temporary push trigger.
cards.landing: Workflow library convention: every script step runnable standalone; supports saving workflows (W5) and debugging

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: whether it can be silently disabled
cards.claim: When choosing a sensor, weigh stability, cost and repeatability and whether the measurement can be silently disabled (e.g. by an inline lint-disable comment); the worked example put the sensor config outside the lint config for this reason.
cards.evidence_detail: React Doctor example: chosen because 'a stray inline comment can't quietly switch it off'.
cards.landing: Verifier/compliance design: a check an agent cannot quietly skip or disable; relevant to 'store never consulted looks like routine skipped'

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: This is the part you **tune over time** from loop output
cards.claim: The controller (what to do now vs defer; which target, how many, in what order) ranges from deterministic script to fully agentic and is the component to tune from loop output; start simple.
cards.evidence_detail: Taxonomy text.
cards.landing: Phase selection / work-queue picker as a tunable script; model routing as the controller's tuning knob

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: don't manufacture separation that isn't there
cards.claim: Components may be fused (sensor+controller, controller+actuator); do not split a loop into discrete steps the design does not have.
cards.evidence_detail: Example collapses all three into one agent step.
cards.landing: Workflow-script design guidance (avoid over-structured multi-agent scripts)

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: stop scheduled runs when an open PR for this loop already exists
cards.claim: Flow control: bound work-in-progress to one open PR per loop (label-gated, scheduled runs no-op, manual dispatch bypasses) so the agent never produces PRs faster than review.
cards.evidence_detail: Rationale: without it a daily agent could stack 5+ unreviewed PRs a week (from build-iterated-agentic-loop).
cards.landing: Phase routine: one open draft PR per phase; owner-review backlog cap before starting next phase

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: a check (often on PRs / pushes to main) that compares the sensor's output against a baseline
cards.claim: Dampener: a regression gate comparing sensor output to a baseline so the measured problem cannot get worse while the loop improves it; advisory by default, graduating to blocking once trusted.
cards.evidence_detail: React Doctor example: advisory by default, comments only on newly introduced issues, documented path to blocking.
cards.landing: CI: ratchet checks (e.g. import-boundary or lint-count baselines) that only fail on new violations; pre-commit gate re-open

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Scope gate** — restrict the actuator to safe directories
cards.claim: Restrict the actuator to safe directories, exclude generated/vendored/high-risk packages, and cap each run by finding/file/package count to keep diffs reviewable.
cards.evidence_detail: Scope gate and batch size listed as extra loop parts; prompt template says 'inspect secondary path only when necessary'.
cards.landing: Per-phase file allow-list in the plan; batch-size caps in workflow scripts; interacts with import-linter contracts

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Keep durable guidance only — not one-off instructions or single-run logs.
cards.claim: A version-controlled memory file of standing feedback (scope exclusions, false positives, reviewer preferences) is loaded deterministically into the actuator on every run, after the controller; good entries are durable, and the test is whether deleting it would lose useful future-run context.
cards.evidence_detail: Memory template; build-iterated-agentic-loop adds 'Completion criterion: deleting the memory file would lose useful future-run context, not just history'. Narrow-props memory example is one line.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store design: separate durable standing guidance from run logs; a short deterministic-load memory file as a cheaper alternative or companion

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Label each loop's PRs and embed a hidden marker
cards.claim: /iterate: a maintainer comments /iterate on the loop's PR; a hidden marker in the PR body routes the comment to the workflow that created it, which loads the diff, comments and feedback and updates both the PR and the memory file; the marker is checked before checkout so non-matching workflows no-op cheaply.
cards.evidence_detail: Implemented in workflow-template.yml gate step and agent-iteration.ts (footer and prompt modes); restricted to OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR comments.
cards.landing: Owner feedback path on a phase PR that updates durable memory, not only the PR; marker-in-PR-body routing as machine-readable provenance

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Put ordered behavior in `SKILL.md` as steps with checkable completion criteria
cards.claim: Write skills as ordered steps each with a checkable completion criterion, push long templates and examples into sibling reference files, and keep one source of truth per rule across skill, prompt and memory.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill-writing rules repeated in design-control-loop and build-iterated-agentic-loop; every phase ends with a 'Completion criterion'.
cards.landing: Skill authoring template for new skills and the phase routine steps: each routine step ends with an observable completion criterion

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Each phase above names the references relevant to it — read each one when you reach that phase.
cards.claim: Progressive disclosure inside a skill: each phase of SKILL.md names exactly which reference files to read at that phase, rather than loading all references up front.
cards.evidence_detail: Every phase begins with 'Read the following references:'. Contrasts with the improve-claude-md advice against sharding CLAUDE.md.
cards.landing: Skill structure and phase routine: per-step reads list; limits context loaded per phase

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: the `name` in the skill's frontmatter must match its directory slug
cards.claim: A skill's frontmatter name must equal its directory slug (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) or it will not resolve.
cards.evidence_detail: Bolded IMPORTANT in both skills.
cards.landing: Checklist for the skills being added; a trivial CI check could enforce it

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: You are running in a sandbox or CI runner environment. Do not stop and ask for feedback
cards.claim: Unattended-agent prompt shape: Context (begin with the named skill), Scope (primary path, secondary only if needed), numbered Instructions (one small reviewable increment, no adjacent cleanup), Validation commands, Important Rules, Finishing Up, and a fixed Output Format that becomes the PR body.
cards.evidence_detail: Template with placeholders; repo-specific targeting lives in the prompt, generic judgement in the skill.
cards.landing: Workflow library: a saved prompt skeleton for headless phase agents; split of repo-specific vs generic content between prompt and skill

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Lead with summary stats - Reviewers should know scope immediately
cards.claim: The agent's final response is a defined template: lead with summary counts, group by resolution (fixed/ignored/skipped), highlight risk levels, give manual verification steps for medium/high risk, keep it scannable.
cards.evidence_detail: Three example templates (fix/migration, generation, refactor). Each issue gets an explicit FIXED, IGNORED (with reason) or SKIPPED (needs human) outcome.
cards.landing: Six-question closing message and per-register-id outcome list; an explicit 'skipped, needs human' outcome makes silent skipping visible

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: three honest options — **fix**, **ignore**
cards.claim: Give the actuator three honest options per finding (fix, ignore with a recorded reason in config, or skip for a human) and validate and commit each change separately.
cards.evidence_detail: React Doctor loop: validates with typecheck, quality, and the sensor on staged files; one commit per issue.
cards.landing: Phase agent and reviewer verdict vocabulary; per-item commits make fail-before/pass-after attributable per register id

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Use `--max-turns` or `--max-budget-usd` when the repo needs spend guards.
cards.claim: Headless Claude Code runs (claude -p) can be bounded with --max-turns or --max-budget-usd; the final assistant message is extracted from stream-json output with jq and used as the PR body; tee all output to a file for debugging.
cards.evidence_detail: Command templates for Claude Code, Codex (--output-last-message), OpenCode, CodeLayer; also states broad permission modes are for trusted isolated runners only.
cards.landing: Headless runs for scheduled audits; saved raw transcript (agent-output) as evidence that a routine step ran

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Check iterate marker to bound work-in-progress
cards.claim: A scheduled agent workflow skeleton with discrete sensor, controller, actuator and extract-PR-body steps, a concurrency group, an actor-authorisation gate on comment triggers, a no-commit-no-PR guard, and an upload of the raw agent output as an artifact.
cards.evidence_detail: Template YAML; model defaults shown are Opus with thinking high for fresh runs and Sonnet for the /iterate path.
cards.landing: Saved workflow/CI template; shows a split of effort by task (full cycle on the stronger model, feedback iteration on the cheaper one) as a small model-routing example

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Golden patterns first. Before automating, establish what a good change looks like
cards.claim: Before automating a migration or cleanup, find the golden patterns in the existing code with the user and encode them in the actuator skill so the agent follows established conventions.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase B4 instruction.
cards.landing: Skill content for migrations/refactors: exemplar file paths named in the skill

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Find 5 react-doctor violations, fix them, and verify typecheck and quality pass.
cards.claim: Define an agent job as one sentence covering what is found, what is changed (fix, migrate, generate, refactor) and how it is validated; if you cannot state it in one sentence the job is not repeatable yet.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 3 'Define the agent job' with three questions and a completion criterion.
cards.landing: Workflow-library entry format: finds / changes / validates one-liner per saved workflow

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Repo-specific targeting in the GitHub Actions prompt, not in the generic skill.
cards.claim: Split content by stability: the skill holds reusable judgement; the workflow prompt holds repo-specific scope, validation commands and memory interpolation; no rule should be repeated in skill, prompt and memory.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 5 (note: design-control-loop later reverses this, saying the skill 'can use repo-specific paths' since it lives in the repo).
cards.landing: Where phase-specific facts live (plan vs skill vs CLAUDE.md); single-source-of-truth rule

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Temporarily add a `push` trigger for the current branch
cards.claim: Dry-run a new scheduled workflow by temporarily adding a push trigger on the branch, watching it run, then removing the trigger; review the PR it opens before trusting it.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 9; reason is workflow_dispatch is unavailable until a first run. Also: validate YAML parses and every referenced path exists.
cards.landing: P1 cold-resume trial analogue: first run of a routine is a deliberate dry run reviewed by a human before it is trusted

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: increase the schedule frequency; widen the controller's batch
cards.claim: Once a loop is tuned and producing consistent output, speed it up by raising frequency, widening batch size, running the cycle N times per run, or running it several times with one PR per teammate.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase H guidance, conditional on consistent high-quality output.
cards.landing: Scaling rule: widen only after a loop's output has been reviewed clean; pairs with one-PR-per-loop bound

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Treat live code paths as the source of truth for the prop contract.
cards.claim: Derive the type contract from non-test, non-Storybook call sites; support code (tests, stories, mocks) is evidence of widening only, and must adapt to the strict contract rather than weaken it.
cards.evidence_detail: Worked actuator skill with 11 steps and a review checklist.
cards.landing: Reasoning model for tests vs production code; parallels CLAUDE.md rule that the web app reads the live API, not mock seeds

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Types should be as strict as possible so code can be as simple as possible.
cards.claim: Every optional prop is another state to handle, test and keep correct; make types strict (required nullable over optional, derive types from live APIs) so defensive fallbacks (?? [], optional-call handlers) can be deleted.
cards.evidence_detail: Anti-patterns list: optional callbacks for stories, default* props for Storybook, accepting multiple API shapes.
cards.landing: Mobile TypeScript strict-typing cleanup loop; example candidate for a saved scheduled workflow

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Focus only on `apps/riptide-ui`; do not make changes in `apps/riptide-cloud`.
cards.claim: The whole standing memory for a working loop is one scope-exclusion line; memory stays minimal and scope-oriented.
cards.evidence_detail: The example memory file contains a single guidance bullet; skill also ends with a Review Checklist of verifiable properties of the diff (types derived from live sites, no inert menu items, shared variants compile).
cards.landing: Calibration for the knowledge-store pilot: a working loop needed one line of standing memory; also a skill-end review checklist as the reviewer's rubric

gaps: Did not read design-control-loop references example-skill.md, skill-template.md, agent-iteration.ts, or build-iterated-agentic-loop's other references (not in my file list); narrow-react-prop-types agent-narrow-component-props.yml and response-template.md also unread.

Per-plugin authorship is not visible in the files: every plugin.json lists the org 'humanlayer'. Authors were assigned from the inventory and the task notes (Kyle for design-control-loop, build-iterated-agentic-loop, narrow-react-prop-types; Dex for improve-claude-md and show-me). I did not read git history, so those assignments are unverified.
visual-pr author is not stated anywhere I read, so it is tagged 'other'; the inventory says only that it was added to humanlayer/skills.
No measured results anywhere in these plugins; all claims are asserted or anecdotal, and the 'few hundred instructions' and '~50 in the system prompt' figures carry no source.
